insights.finding: The new swap UI (B) lifts quote→submit conversion from 51.3% to 56.5% (+10.3% relative, p=3e-11, 95% CI [+3.7%, +6.8%])
insights.evidence: User-level analysis, A=7,932 / B=7,900 quoting users; SRM check p=0.75 (assignment healthy); MDE=2.2%.
insights.hypothesis: The route preview reduces uncertainty about slippage and price, so fewer users abandon after quoting.
insights.action: Ship B to 100%. Next experiment: show a gas estimate and a retry flow for failed transactions (the submit→confirm step).
insights.impact: About +2,000 successful swaps per month, ≈ +$2.62M volume / +$7,848 LP fees.

insights.finding: 13% of wallets acquired in July (quest campaign) are sybils; they took 25% of the airdrop and sold 100% of it within 24h (genuine users sold only 32% within 7 days)
insights.evidence: 8 funding clusters with 799 wallets: seeded by one address within <2h, never used the front-end, ~$30 per swap, active <1 month. DEMO price moved -22% in the week after the airdrop.
insights.hypothesis: Points were awarded per transaction count, so scripted farming cost almost nothing.
insights.action: Run funding-cluster and behaviour filters before the airdrop; weight points by fees paid and holding time, with a cap; switch to linear vesting (e.g. 30 days) or tie unlocks to continued activity.
insights.impact: Filtering sybils would redirect ~6.5M DEMO (≈ $245k at distribution) to real users and reduce first-week sell pressure.

insights.finding: Twitter Ads CAC is $56 while 30-day LTV (fees) is only $5.50; quest-platform D30 retention is 50%, well below organic at 86%
insights.evidence: Channel attribution = UTM channel of the session in which the wallet first connected; LTV = LP fees generated in the 30 days after the first swap.
insights.hypothesis: Paid channels bring one-off, task-driven users; organic and KOL users arrive with real trading intent.
insights.action: Move part of the Twitter budget to KOL referrals paid on retention (CPA); redesign quests around retention, e.g. 'trade every week for 4 weeks'.
insights.impact: Every paid channel is below 1× LTV/CAC. Re-evaluate on 90-day LTV and protocol revenue before continuing spend.

insights.finding: Passive LPs in WETH-USDC underperformed holding: fee yield 1.17%, impermanent loss -3.52%, net -2.35% vs HODL
insights.evidence: Daily volume/TVL is only 2.52%. Covering IL would need ~$1.7M average daily volume; actual was $0.57M.
insights.hypothesis: Liquidity is over-provisioned relative to trading demand (low capital efficiency), so LP returns are thin and capital is at risk of leaving.
insights.action: Evaluate concentrated liquidity (V3-style ranges) or dynamic fees; shift DEMO incentives from subsidising TVL to subsidising real volume (trading rewards with wash-trading filters).
insights.impact: Better capital efficiency gives deeper quotes from the same TVL and raises LP APR.

insights.finding: TVL fell -30% on 2026-09-12: a single market maker withdrew half of WETH-USDC liquidity at once
insights.evidence: That address supplied 53% of all WETH-USDC deposits; the robust z-score detector fired the same day.
insights.hypothesis: TVL depends heavily on one market maker; if their strategy changes, slippage and user experience degrade immediately.
insights.action: Alert when any single LP exceeds 30% of a pool; agree lock-ups or staged withdrawals with market makers; use incentives to attract a broader LP base.
insights.impact: Reduces tail risk: a withdrawal during peak trading would sharply widen slippage on large trades.

insights.finding: ~$4.5M of volume over 3 days in early September came from 2 wallets with the same funder wash-trading the DEMO pool
insights.evidence: Both wallets net position / gross volume < 1%, 150 round trips per day, funded by the same address.
insights.hypothesis: Likely an attempt to inflate DEMO volume rankings, or to dress up metrics ahead of a CEX listing.
insights.action: Use 'clean' metrics (excluding bots, sybils and wash trading) for both external reporting and internal KPIs; apply wash filters to leaderboards and incentive calculations.
insights.impact: Reported peak DAU was 1,260 (2026-08-01) versus 461 clean users that day; the gap would mislead decisions.

insights.finding: 27% of real users traded on a single day only; retention is 33% after week 1 and 11% by week 8
insights.evidence: Weekly cohorts by first-swap week, excluding bots, sybils and wash-trading wallets.
insights.hypothesis: After the first trade there is little reason to come back (no limit orders, no portfolio or P&L view).
insights.action: Launch limit orders / DCA and a 'My positions' page; re-engage wallets that haven't returned 7 days after their first swap (e.g. Push Protocol, email).
insights.impact: Each +5pp of week-1 retention adds several hundred monthly active traders at the current acquisition rate.
